name: Algae
lede: Algae is a clear, mid-light green named for the pond and sea plants it brings to mind, though most algae are not this color at all.

sections.title: The name
sections.body: The name comes to us from the 2010 xkcd color survey, as one of the named greens [1]. No book I read treats it as a color word, and who first used it as one is undocumented. ISCC-NBS 1955 would call it a vivid green, 6.6 units away, and its Munsell notation is 1.3G 6.2/8.1 [1]. Close neighbours are [[jade]], [[peppermint]] and [[boring-green]], each a few units off [1].

sections.title: Why algae are green, and often not
sections.body:
Chlorophyll a is carried by every plant, alga and cyanobacterium that photosynthesises, and chlorophyll b by the green algae and land plants only [2]. That shared chemistry is why a green alga and a leaf both read as [[green]] [2]. Gurney adds that algae growth gives freshwater lakes a greenish look [3].

Other groups wear other colors. Paterson lists fucoxanthin, which makes algae brown, phycocyanin, a blue pigment, and phycoerythrin, which reflects red [4]. He also credits the red pigment with the name of the Red Sea, while allowing that blooms of cyanobacteria may be the real reason [4]. Kelps and diatoms carry a third chlorophyll, chlorophyll c [2].

sections.title: The white of algae
sections.body: The most famous algal color is white. Chalk is built from the remains of single-celled marine algae, coccolithophores, laid down as sediment and compacted over millions of years, and it forms the white cliffs of Dover [5][6].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Only two of 23,781 paintings in our archive carry a color within six ΔE units of this green over at least five per cent of the canvas, both by Van Gogh: [[painting:nga-72328|Roses]] and [[painting:nga-163323|Green Wheat Fields, Auvers]], both 1890 [7]. In printed English the word algae peaks around 1978 [8]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match is a screen color and not a pigment test [7].

questions.q: What are the white cliffs of Dover mainly made of?
True or false: all algae are green.

openers: The white cliffs of Dover are made of the remains of single-celled algae.
Brown, blue and red algae exist: pigments such as fucoxanthin and phycoerythrin do the coloring.
